newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia police cuts refugee smuggle chain.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia police cuts refugee smuggle chain.

text.p: Bosnian police cracked down on Monday on attempts to smuggle Turkish Kurds to Western Europe.
About 90 Turkish citizens, believed to be Kurds, left Sarajevo by air for Turkey after being taken to the airport in police vehicles.
Turks can enter Bosnia without a visa and stay up to three months. Police said those who returned home on Monday left voluntarily after realising they were not going to get any further without visas.
A Turkish embassy official who translated for police said that the Kurds had paid up to 4,000 German marks ($2,500) each to a syndicate which promised them passage to Western Europe.
"I understood they were using Bosnia, Croatia and Slovenia to enter Italy, Austria and Germany," the official said.

A police source who asked not to be identified told Reuters: "They (Turkish Kurds) began arriving in Sarajevo in February in small numbers when a direct flight to Istanbul was established, but we got suspicious recently when too many arrived.
"We are currently working on cutting this chain of smuggling people to Austria, Italy and Germany."
